audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart said Ornn owns Levels 2 and 3 and that Level 6 is 'Skill'. The content-layer whys, and the packet levelChart, say the opposite: Level 2 is a farm standoff, Level 3 is Aatrox's window, Level 6 is Ornn's.
audit.why: At 3 Aatrox has The Darkin Blade sweetspot (14s at rank 1) plus Infernal Chains and Deathbringer Stance healing before Ornn's Bellows Breath is meaningful. At 6 Call of the Forge God knocks up on approach and again on the recast, and World Ender is a stat steroid that does nothing while airborne.
audit.corrected: Rows 1,2,4 flipped in matched pairs across both layers: L2 Skill, L3 Aatrox, L6 Ornn.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why described level 6 generically and hedged that Aatrox's ultimate 'changes the math'.
audit.why: World Ender grants AD, healing and move speed; none of it functions while knocked up by Call of the Forge God's charge and recast.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the double knockup and why World Ender loses to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of anti-heal despite three healing sources, and no mention of the Deathbringer Stance auto-attack reset as the combo tell. Cooldown block gave no numbers.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance (P), Umbral Dash (E) and World Ender (R) all heal; Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. The combo opens on an auto reset, so the wind-up is the cue, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d now names the three healing sources and calls for Grievous Wounds; breakdown.cooldowns now gives The Darkin Blade's 14s/6s and the Deathbringer Stance wind-up tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns tracked The Darkin Blade with no duration.
audit.why: Real cooldowns make the advice actionable: 14/12/10/8/6.

edits.before: W brittle turns every trade into bonus %HP damage. Only take the trade when Aatrox's The Darkin Blade is down.
edits.after: Bellows Breath is not up yet and his Darkin Blade sweetspot is not online either, so level 2 stays a farm standoff.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aatrox must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: At 3 his Darkin Blade sweetspot knockup into Infernal Chains plus passive healing out-trades you — hold the wave and last-hit.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aatrox's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God knocks him up on the charge and again on the recast, and World Ender's AD and healing do nothing while he is airborne — 6 is yours.

edits.before: Sweetspots knock up. Sidestep them. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Sweetspot knocks up. Sidestep it — at rank 1 it is down 14s, and that is your window.

edits.before: E-dashing with no terrain in the line — no knockup means you delivered yourself to his combo for free.
edits.after: Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash and World Ender all heal him — bring Grievous Wounds before extended trades.

edits.before: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: matchup-defining — Sweetspots knock up. Sidestep them. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - The Darkin Blade: 14s at rank 1, 6s at rank 5 — sweetspots knock up, so sidestep and engage while it is down. - Deathbringer Stance: the auto wind-up is the tell, step back on it. - Your R: kill windows only.

notes: Level chart was internally consistent between layers but contradicted both the packet chart and its own whys text; flipped three rows in matched full/content pairs. dontsFull[2] ('Skip anti-heal') had a body copied verbatim from the bad-trade line — it never mentioned anti-heal at all; replaced with the real healing sources.
